bedtime: A mother in a dark dress holds her small daughter on her lap in a quiet, tender moment at the end of the day. Paul Peel, a Canadian painter who became a star in Paris, was famous for warm pictures of home and childhood. The soft light and gentle pose make it feel cozy. It's a sweet picture of love at bedtime.
in-the-shade-of-the-apple-tree: A young woman sits quietly in the dappled shade of an apple tree on a sunny day. Horatio Walker painted the countryside of Quebec, where he lived much of the year. The soft light and calm mood are typical of his peaceful style. It's a restful country scene.
morning-milking: A cow stands beside a fence in a soft, misty farmyard in the early morning. Horatio Walker was known as the painter of Quebec farm life, and he sold many paintings in the United States. The gentle light and quiet mood are typical of his style. It's a peaceful rural scene.
brise-d-ete-a-dinard: People stroll and rest on a sunny beach with colorful parasols and striped beach tents at the seaside resort of Dinard in France. Clarence Gagnon painted this in his early career, when he was studying in Paris. The bright sand and sea are lively. It's a happy summer day at the beach.
ole: A dancer in a bright red dress stands with her arm raised in a flamenco pose, while a guitarist plays beside her. Clarence Gagnon, a Quebec painter, traveled widely in Europe and painted scenes from Spain. The title is the Spanish shout of praise, 'Olé!' It shows that Canadian artists also painted the world.
behind-bonsecours-market-montreal: A busy market square beside the harbor of Montreal is filled with shoppers, carts and sailing ships. William Raphael, born in Prussia, settled in Montreal and painted its streets and markets. His pictures record what the city looked like in the 1860s. It's a historic snapshot of Montreal.
chippewas-hunting-caribou: Anishinaabe (Chippewa) hunters track caribou through the woods and along a stream. Cornelius Krieghoff painted this to show life he'd seen in the northern wilderness. The trees and small figures show how large the land was. It's an important image of Indigenous hunting.
canoe-on-the-river: A small round painting shows a quiet river framed by trees in glowing autumn colors. Cornelius Krieghoff painted the glorious color of the Canadian fall, which became a favorite subject. The round shape makes it feel like looking through a window. It's a peaceful picture of autumn.
beacon-light-saint-john-harbour: A sailing ship glows in dim, hazy light near the harbor of Saint John, New Brunswick. Henry Sandham painted Atlantic Canada's ports and coasts in a clear, careful way. The soft light on the water gives the scene a quiet mood. It's a calm harbor view.
biskra: A sunny, dry riverbed in the oasis town of Biskra in Algeria, with a faraway ridge and a few small figures. Maurice Cullen, a Montreal painter, traveled to North Africa and painted its vivid colors. He is best known for his snowy Canadian winter scenes. It's an unusual desert view by a painter of snow.
interesting-story: Two girls snuggle together on a sofa over a big book, absorbed in an exciting story. Laura Muntz Lyall was a Canadian painter from Toronto who became well known for her gentle pictures of children. She painted in a soft, delicate style and exhibited in Paris and London. It's a cozy picture of reading together.
self-portrait-emily-carr: Emily Carr is shown at her easel in a room with strong, simple shapes and bold colors. She was one of Canada's greatest painters, who lived much of her life in British Columbia with her pet monkey, dogs and her paintbrushes. She wasn't widely recognized until she was in her fifties, when the Group of Seven discovered her art. It's a picture of an artist at work.
dreams: A young woman lies in the grass above the sea, lost in daydreams. Jozef Israëls, a Dutch painter of Jewish background, was the leader of the Hague School and often painted quiet, thoughtful moments. The soft light and dreamy pose invite you to wonder what she is thinking. It's a gentle picture of imagination.
portrait-of-the-painter-oda-krohg-b-lass: A woman in a red blouse stands confidently with her hands on her hips. Oda Krohg was a painter herself and Christian Krohg's wife, and an important figure in the Kristiania art world. Her husband painted her several times. It's a lively tribute from one artist to another.
karen-inga-basker-werenskiold: A young girl in a fur-trimmed coat and cap looks calmly out of the picture. Erik Werenskiold painted his family and close friends with honesty. He was one of the most respected Norwegian painters and also illustrated Norwegian fairy tales. It's an affectionate family portrait.
kunstnerviften: A folding fan painted with little portraits of artist friends. Asta Nørregaard, one of Norway's first professional women painters, worked in Kristiania (now Oslo) and was a supporter of other artists. A fan like this was a playful gift to remember friends. It's an unusual and charming piece of art.
dinner: A woman sits at a table in a modern room beside a window with a view of the sea. Léon Bakst was a Jewish artist from Russia, best known for designing amazing costumes and sets for the Ballets Russes in Paris. His sense of color and mood made even simple scenes feel like a stage. This early work shows his stylish touch.
coffee-table: A richly decorated Ottoman room, with a low table, rugs and a few people in colorful robes. Osman Hamdi Bey was a leading Ottoman painter and also the founder of Turkey's first archaeological museum. He painted objects and patterns with the same care he gave to his scientific work. It's a window into a Turkish home.
ahasuerus: A close portrait of a weary, noble-looking man with a faraway gaze: the legendary Wandering Jew, a man condemned to roam forever. Maurycy Gottlieb painted Ahasuerus with dignity instead of horror, giving a sad folk legend a feeling of grandeur. It shows how Jewish artists reworked old stories. It's a powerful, quiet portrait.
helvig-paus: A girl in a white dress with long red hair looks calmly out of the picture. Eilif Peterssen painted many portraits of leading Norwegians and their families. This one comes from late in his career. It's a gentle, graceful portrait.
portrait-of-marguerite-van-mons: A young girl in a dark dress stands in a doorway, painted with tiny dots of color. Théo van Rysselberghe, a Belgian painter, used the pointillist technique, which makes the light sparkle. The dots blend together when you step back. It's a lovely portrait of a child.
maria-sethe: A woman in a rich purple dress sits at a piano, painted with bright strokes of color. Théo van Rysselberghe painted Maria Sèthe, who later became the wife of the Belgian architect Henry van de Velde. The picture glows with color and music. It's a charming portrait.
storks: Two farmers rest in a green field with their oxen while storks wander nearby. Józef Chełmoński, a Polish painter, was famous for painting birds and the Polish countryside. White storks come to Poland every summer and are loved as a symbol of good luck. It's a charming picture of country life.
a-rose: A woman in a rose-pink gown sits in a quiet pose, painted with soft, warm color. Thomas Pollock Anshutz was a Philadelphia painter and teacher who taught many famous artists at the Pennsylvania Academy of the Fine Arts. He painted this late in his career. It's a delicate, gentle portrait.
armour: Geometric shapes in gray, black and white are stacked into an abstract design that looks like a suit of armor. Ragnhild Keyser was a Norwegian painter, among the first women in Norway to study art abroad, and she explored modern styles. The picture is strong, simple and bold. It's an interesting piece of modern Norwegian art.
gossamer: A young woman rests in a meadow in the golden light of early autumn, with geese grazing nearby and silvery spider threads floating in the air. Józef Chełmoński painted this in 1875, and Poles call it 'Babie lato' (Indian summer). It is one of Poland's most beloved paintings. The glowing light is magical.
woman-with-a-sunflower: A mother holds her child close in a bright, sunny scene, with a big sunflower. Mary Cassatt painted this late in her career with a bold, colorful touch. She became famous for pictures of mothers and children. It's a warm, joyful family picture.
summer-fun: A young woman in a white dress sits in a boat on a calm, sparkling bay in Sweden, painted in glowing summer light. Anders Zorn, one of Sweden's most celebrated painters, was famous for watercolors and for showing sparkling light on water. He loved to paint his country's countryside and its people. It's a cheerful summer scene.
omnibus: A woman in black sits quietly on a horse-drawn omnibus in Paris, looking down in thought. Anders Zorn painted this scene of city life in 1892, with great skill at catching light and shadow. It's a snapshot of everyday travel in the city. It's a quiet slice of Paris.
